title: Document permissions support group-based access control and operation-level restrictions, stored across six database tables
content:
Permission resolution order: (1) Auth/admin check; (2) Direct user permission on document; (3) Group permission; (4) Parent inheritance recursively. Six tables: `DocumentPermission` (user-document), `Group`, `UserGroup` (memberships), `DocumentGroupPermission` (group-document), `OperationUserPermission` (user-operation), `OperationGroupPermission` (group-operation). Operation-level permissions restrict specific actions (e.g., only certain users can execute DELETE_NODE). Tables are auto-created by migrations when `DOCUMENT_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED=true`. GraphQL queries like `documentAccess`, `userDocumentPermissions`, `canExecuteOperation` expose the permission state.

## Stale as of v6.2.2-dev.74
The six-table shape and the group-based access control described here came from the Academy's Document Permissions page, which still documents groups — but the code does not have them. `packages/reactor-api/src/migrations/003_remove_group_tables.ts` drops `Group`, `UserGroup`, `DocumentGroupPermission` and `OperationGroupPermission`, and grepping `group` across `packages/reactor-api/src/graphql/auth/` returns zero hits. **Three** tables survive: `DocumentPermission`, `OperationUserPermission` and `DocumentProtection`. The permission-resolution order (auth/admin check, direct user permission, parent inheritance) still holds with the group step removed. Treat the page as stale and the migration as authoritative.
description: Groups organize users; permissions cascade from drive to folder to document; specific operations can be restricted.
